 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Jones, who strained his left hamstring early in training camp, is also navigating a right hamstring injury. His absence may give fellow reserve Trevon Brazile a few minutes, but it is unlikely to significantly affect fantasy basketball.

 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Due to a strained left hamstring, Jones did not play at all during the preseason. He’s on the injury report for Denver’s season opener due to bilateral hamstring injury management, so his right hamstring is also a concern. If Jones can’t play, the Nuggets may have to rely on rookie Trevon Brazile a little more, with the second-round pick coming off a productive preseason. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) said on Sunday that he expects to be available for Thursday’s opener against the Thunder. 
 Jones strained his left hamstring early in training camp and did not play in any of the Nuggets’ preseason games. He’s made positive strides in his recovery, most recently doing some scrimmaging during Sunday’s practice. Following the session, Jones said that he expects to be available for Sunday’s opener. If Jones plays, there may be fewer minutes available to rookie Trevon Brazile, who played well in the Nuggets’ final preseason games. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 12 points (5-of-7 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 With Aaron Gordon sitting out Friday’s preseason finale, the Nuggets inserted Brazile into the starting lineup. The rookie, who dropped 22 points on Wednesday against the Clippers, had another solid outing to end his first preseason. Brazile may not play heavy minutes, but he’s clearly done enough to crack the Nuggets’ rotation right away. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers. 
 The 35th overall pick in this past summer’s draft, Brazile had his most productive night of the preseason on Wednesday. The 6-foot-10 forward/center shot 80 percent from the field, and his final line lacked only an assist. Based on playing time, Brazile has already leapfrogged former first-round picks Zeke Nnaji and DaRon Holmes II in the frontcourt pecking order. He may not get the minutes needed to impact fantasy basketball once the regular season begins, but Brazile needs to be rostered in dynasty leagues. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile finished Sunday’s 109-97 loss to the Jazz with seven points, three rebounds, two blocked shots and a triple across 20 minutes. 
 The rookie out of Arkansas tied Julian Strawther for team lead in minutes, and he had a serviceable night, going 3-of-4 from the field and making an impact on defense. Denver doesn’t boast a deep bench, especially in the frontcourt, so Brazile has a real chance to earn meaningful rotation minutes in Year 1. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Nuggets are matching the Thunder’s offer sheet, keeping Spencer Jones on a two-year contract. 
 The Nuggets’ decision to match the Thunder’s offer sheet comes less than 48 hours after OKC’s initial offer. Jones, who averaged 5.5 points and 3.3 rebounds across 64 games last regular season, should remain a solid piece off Denver’s bench for the 2026-27 campaign. He’s mostly a three-point specialist who can provide some perimeter defense as well during his minutes, but is unlikely to move high enough up Denver’s depth chart to have any fantasy value next season. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones has agreed to a two-year, $12 million offer sheet with the Thunder, reports NBA Insider Michael Scotto. 
 Jones is a restricted free agent, so the Nuggets still have the opportunity to match the contract and keep him. If not, this was a wise bit of maneuvering by the Thunder as they were able to offer Jones using the Taxpayer mid-level exception after getting under the second apron by trading Lu Dort. Jones averaged 5.5 points in 22.5 minutes per game during the regular season last year, but stepped up during the playoffs, shooting 69 percent from three-point range. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile notched 17 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Brazile did not have his best night shooting the basketball, but the second-round pick still showed why Denver made sure to draft him. Active on the glass and defensively, the 6-foot-10 forward finished with another solid stat line. Like fellow second-round pick Bryce Hopkins, Brazile has not yet agreed to a contract, with Peyton Watson’s free agency likely a factor. However, he has the potential to contribute immediately for the Nuggets because of his athleticism and motor. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 32 points (11-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one steal, one block and six three-pointers. 
 Brazile put forth his best performance of the summer on Tuesday, and he was on fire from the start. The second-round pick scored 19 points in the first half, ending it with a long three from just inside the half-court line as time expired. Brazile would score 13 more after halftime, more than holding his own against a Thunder frontcourt headlined by lottery pick Aday Mara. Because of Peyton Watson’s restricted free agency, Brazile’s contract status has not been finalized, but games like Tuesday’s likely increase his chances of landing a standard deal. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile tallied five points (2-of-8 FGs), 11 rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Brazile made his first summer league appearance on Friday, and he struggled to finish around the basket. The former Arkansas forward/center shot 2-of-7 from two, but he was active on the boards with a game-high 11 rebounds. Like fellow rookie Bryce Hopkins, Brazile has not finalized a contract as the Nuggets attend to other affairs, most notably Peyton Watson’s restricted free agency. With DaRon Holmes II a full year removed from his Achilles tear and Zeke Nnaji yet to pan out, there may be opportunities for Brazile off the bench, mainly as a defender and rebounder.

 Joel Embiid said after Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers that he will miss one of the 76ers’ final two games of the week.
 The 76ers were the only team with a four-game Week 1, which will conclude with a Saturday-Sunday back-to-back. Embiid sitting out one game of a back-to-back, especially this early in the season, is not a surprise. The only issue is that he didn’t reveal which game he’ll miss, with the 76ers hosting Milwaukee on Saturday and Detroit on Sunday. Given the strength of those teams, the Bucks may be the team that misses out on having to deal with “The Process.” Adem Bona or Jabari Walker could get a spot start, and LeBron James may spend a little more time at center as a small-ball alternative.

 DeMar DeRozan produced 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs) and two rebounds in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
 DeRozan was used in a reserve role on Thursday, and that’s likely how he’ll be used on nights when the Nuggets are healthy. More importantly, he got 28 minutes in his Nuggets debut. DeRozan’s issues on Thursday: foul shooting and turnovers. In addition to missing three of six from the charity stripe, DeRozan recorded five turnovers. He’s averaged more than 2.5 turnovers per game once in his NBA career, so fantasy managers shouldn’t worry about Thursday’s number. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Aaron Gordon tallied 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
 A notoriously poor perimeter shooter for most of his NBA career, Gordon has worked hard in recent years to change that. A 41 percent three-point shooter over his last two seasons, the Nuggets forward hit 3-of-4 from distance on Thursday. By comparison, the other starters shot a combined 3-of-15 from beyond the arc against the Thunder. No one should expect Gordon to challenge Stephen Curry, but his perimeter shot is no longer a liability. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cameron Johnson (ankle) finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with five points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
 Johnson played 11 minutes in Thursday’s opener before a right ankle injury ended his night just before halftime. Officially, the veteran wing was questionable for the second half, but he never returned. Alpha Diallo (4/2/3/1) started the second half and played 22 minutes. If Nuggets head coach David Adelman prefers to keep DeMar DeRozan in the sixth man role, Diallo could start Saturday’s game against the Pelicans if Johnson can’t play.

 Christian Braun amassed seven points (3-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
 While injuries played a role last season, Braun’s scoring average dropped by more than three points compared to his 2024-25 output. Unfortunately, the Nuggets guard got off to a slow start on Thursday, shooting 3-of-10 from the field. Braun was active on the glass, but the overall production was disappointing.

 Jamal Murray recorded six points (2-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
 Murray shot 2-of-9 from the field in the first half of Thursday’s season opener. Unfortunately for fantasy managers who likely believed that things couldn’t get worse in the second half, they did. Murray scored just one point after halftime and recorded more turnovers (four) than field-goal attempts (two). With the Nuggets playing just two games during Week 1, fantasy managers will hope to see Murray rebound on Saturday against the Pelicans.

 Nikola Jokić accounted for 13 points (5-of-19 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss ot the Thunder.
 Neither MVP winner in Thursday’s game played well in the first half. The difference was that while Oklahoma City’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander turned things around in the second half, Jokić could not. The Thunder big men deserve credit for their defense, but “The Joker” couldn’t find a rhythm. He and the Nuggets will look to bounce back when they host the Pelicans on Saturday.

 Ajay Mitchell amassed 12 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five steals and one blocked shot in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
 While he may not be in the Thunder’s starting lineup, Mitchell can still provide solid fantasy value. He played 24 minutes against the Nuggets, doubling his point total from Tuesday’s win over the Spurs. More important for fantasy managers were the “stocks": Mitchell tallied six steals and blocks after recording none in San Antonio. Five-steal nights are unlikely to be the norm, but Mitchell can be close to a top-100 fantasy player for a second consecutive season.

 Chet Holmgren recorded 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 17 rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
 After blocking four shots in Tuesday’s season opener, Holmgren matched that mark on Thursday night. Add in the rebounds, and this was an excellent night for those rostering the slender 7-footer, especially in category leagues. The Western Conference Finals may have left a bad taste in Holmgren’s mouth, but he appears to have put that behind him. This could be a big season for Holmgren if he stays healthy.

 Jalen Williams accounted for 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
 J-Dub was Oklahoma City’s top scorer in their home opener, leading the team with 21 points while shooting just under 50 percent from the field. Williams, who appeared in just 33 games last season, looked much sharper than he did in Tuesday’s season-opening win over the Spurs. If he stays healthy, J-Dub should deliver a top-50 season to fantasy managers at a minimum.
